data.title: Porokeratosis — viva
data.summary: Disorders of keratinisation · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Porokeratosis** (Disorders of keratinisation)_

**Q1. What is porokeratosis?**
- Group of clonal disorders of keratinisation characterised clinically by annular plaques with a thread-like raised keratotic rim and histologically by the cornoid lamella; defects in the mevalonate pathway (MVK, PMVK, MVD, FDPS genes) with second-hit somatic mutation in lesions

**Q2. Describe the types and clinical features (PYQ).**
- Porokeratosis of Mibelli (classic): one or few plaques with a raised furrowed keratotic ridge and atrophic centre, childhood, limbs
- Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis (DSAP): commonest; multiple small (5–10 mm) annular brownish lesions on sun-exposed extensor limbs, adults; worsens in summer/immunosuppression
- Disseminated superficial porokeratosis (non-actinic — also sun-protected sites; immunosuppressed)
- Linear porokeratosis (along Blaschko's lines — highest malignancy risk)
- Porokeratosis palmaris et plantaris disseminata (palms/soles then generalised)
- Punctate porokeratosis (palms/soles), genitogluteal/ptychotropic, hypertrophic verrucous, eruptive (paraneoplastic/inflammatory), porokeratotic eccrine ostial and dermal duct naevus (PEODDN)

**Q3. What is a cornoid lamella?**
- Thin column of tightly packed parakeratotic cells angled away from the centre, arising from an invagination of epidermis with absent/reduced granular layer and dyskeratotic cells at its base — corresponds to the raised rim
- Also seen focally in actinic keratosis, verrucae, seborrhoeic keratosis (not diagnostic alone)

**Q4. Malignant potential.**
- SCC (also BCC, Bowen's) develops in ~7–11% — highest in linear and large long-standing lesions (Mibelli), lowest in DSAP; immunosuppression increases risk

**Q5. Enumerate disorders of transepidermal elimination (PYQ).**
- Primary perforating disorders: Kyrle's disease, perforating folliculitis, reactive perforating collagenosis, elastosis perforans serpiginosa (Down syndrome, penicillamine, Ehlers–Danlos, Marfan), acquired perforating dermatosis (diabetes + chronic renal failure)
- Secondary: granuloma annulare (perforating), necrobiosis lipoidica, pseudoxanthoma elasticum, calcinosis cutis, chondrodermatitis, gout, foreign bodies, chromoblastomycosis, porokeratosis

**Q6. Differential diagnosis.**
- DSAP vs actinic keratosis, lichen planus (annular/atrophic), tinea corporis, granuloma annulare, seborrhoeic keratosis, Bowen's, elastosis perforans serpiginosa; linear porokeratosis vs linear epidermal naevus/linear LP

**Q7. Treatment.**
- Photoprotection, regular skin surveillance (biopsy any nodules/ulcers)
- Topical: 5-FU, imiquimod, vitamin D analogues, retinoids, diclofenac, lovastatin 2% + cholesterol 2% (topical statin–cholesterol — targets mevalonate pathway; newer effective option)
- Physical: cryotherapy, CO2/Er:YAG/fractional lasers, PDT, curettage, excision of small lesions
- Oral acitretin for extensive disease/chemoprevention

**Q8. What is the genetic basis?**
- Mevalonate pathway genes — MVK, PMVK, MVD, FDPS (germline heterozygous mutation + second-hit/ UV-induced somatic mutation); explains DSAP worsening with UV and topical cholesterol/lovastatin therapy

**Q9. Dermoscopy of porokeratosis.**
- White-yellow 'double-edged' track-like peripheral rim (cornoid lamella) — 'white track' around a central brown/pink atrophic area with dotted vessels

**Q10. What is the newer topical treatment?**
- Topical 2% cholesterol + 2% lovastatin (or simvastatin) — corrects mevalonate pathway deficiency (bypasses toxic metabolite accumulation and supplies cholesterol); effective in DSAP and linear porokeratosis

## Quick spotter facts
- Annular plaque with thread-like keratotic ridge — porokeratosis; cornoid lamella
- Linear porokeratosis — highest SCC risk
- Topical lovastatin–cholesterol

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Porokeratosis). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
